attribution.note: Marcus's own retrospective in his Substack post, written in the first person.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps 'appear to have been confirmed' and keeps the insider comments as the basis for his judgment. It is a retrospective observation about Nov–Dec 2024, not a forecast.

contract.note: Reading the claim as tentative corroboration from insider testimony, not proof of a ceiling, is ordinary and fair. Separating pretraining limits from inference-time scaling matches 'pure scaling'.

evidence.note: Reuters report of Nov 11, 2024: Sutskever says pretraining scaling results have plateaued, and three sources describe disappointing training runs at major labs.
At NeurIPS on Dec 13, 2024, Sutskever said pretraining as we know it will end and that data has peaked. This is consistent with diminishing returns, not an exhausted ceiling.
Amodei, in Nov 2024, still backed scaling, partly through new methods. This shows insiders disagreed but does not refute the comments Marcus cited.

reviews.rationale: Reputable reporting in Nov–Dec 2024 records prominent insiders, chiefly Sutskever, plus several unnamed lab sources, describing a plateau or limits in scaling pretraining. That meets the contract's bar of tentative, multi-source corroboration. Amodei's dissent shows there was no consensus, but Marcus claimed only that the prediction 'appears' confirmed.

attribution.note: Marcus's own first-person retrospective on his December 2022 predictions.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps 'largely', the exception for prediction seven, and the universal scope 'every model released in 2024'.

contract.note: Treating 'largely' as the overall pattern holding, and 'every model' as relevant general-purpose 2024 models, is a fair reading. Because the claim is universal, it needs broad coverage.

evidence.note: GSM-Symbolic (Oct 2024) finds fragile mathematical reasoning across the models tested, including GPT-4o and o1 variants. This covers one prediction for a subset of models.
OpenAI's own system card reports nonzero hallucination rates for five models from 2024, alongside improvements. It covers only the hallucination prediction.
HELM Safety finds jailbreak weaknesses in selected Claude, GPT and Llama models, partly supporting the predictions about safeguards and alignment.
Structured Outputs reaches 100% schema compliance, but OpenAI says the values can still be wrong. This qualifies, but does not refute, the prediction about downstream software use.

reviews.rationale: The evidence supports parts of the reasoning, hallucination and safeguard predictions for selected models. There is no inventory of the models released in 2024, and no matched evaluation of all six predictions for those models. The contract says selected tests cannot establish the universal claim, so the packet does not settle it.

attribution.note: Marcus's own prediction, listed under 'High confidence'.

semantics.note: 'Will continue throughout the year', filed as high confidence, is an unqualified forecast for calendar 2025.

contract.note: The plain reading (litigation still ongoing across 2025, including at year-end) is ordinary and requires neither new filings nor plaintiff wins.

evidence.note: SDNY order of May 2025 in the OpenAI copyright MDL records a discovery conference on Jan 22, 2025 and shows litigation still active in May.
SDNY order of Dec 15, 2025 lets Ziff Davis's claims against OpenAI go forward in part.
Plaintiffs' filing of Dec 29, 2025 in the MDL shows proceedings still active at year-end.

reviews.rationale: Court records show generative-AI copyright litigation against OpenAI active in January, May and mid-to-late December 2025. The forecast that such lawsuits would continue throughout 2025 came true.

attribution.note: Marcus's own first-person retrospective claim that Sora's physics problems persisted.

semantics.note: 'They haven't' asserts that the physics problems persisted from February 2024 to the time of writing (end of 2024). Treating it as an observation is right.

contract.note: The plain reading (unrealistic physics was still a limitation at end-2024, not every output failing) is ordinary and fair.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own technical report of Feb 15, 2024 admits the model fails to model basic physical interactions. This establishes the starting limitation.
OpenAI's launch notice of Dec 9, 2024 says the deployed Sora Turbo often generates unrealistic physics. It is a company disclosure, but it admits a limitation.

reviews.rationale: OpenAI's own documentation records physics failures in the February 2024 model and again in the version deployed in December 2024. The packet has no evidence that the problem was solved by the end of 2024.
